main_text.l: tasse[?] illud Pauli afferat, Rom.14.verf.5. Quisque abundat in suo sensu. quod plane alio pertinet, neque ad hunc errorem confirmandū facit. Sed & quod hæretici, ut docet Hilarius in libro ad Constantium, iam ad suos errores defendendos autoritate scripturæ passim niti videbantur, magnum huius Rhetorianorū erroris fundamentū vel fulcimentū fuit. Jovinianus imperator perpe-rā[?] laudatur à Themistio, quòd libera esse cuiusque hæretici religione fiverit[?]. Istud tamen Rhetorianorū cogitari, nedum dici non potuit, nisi propter allegorias in Scripturæ interpretatione iam inductas, homines exististimassent in scripto Dei verbo nihil certū, nihilque definitū inesse, sed velut nasum cereum à quoque, pro animi sui sensu in varias & contrarias partes & sententias torqueri posse. Hanc igitur de sacræ Scripturæ dubia & ancipiti intelligentia opinionem non modò hæreticam esse pronuntiat hoc loco Augustinus: sed etiam stupedam & [illegible, ~6 letters], quam tamen Papistæ tuentur, & in primis literis Clementis Romani pontificis, de Synodo Tridentina colligenda datis, diserte totidemque pene literis retulerunt, & descripserunt. Quo autem tempore collocanda sit hæc hæreticorum familia, ignoro, nisi post Apellitas, & post annum à Christo passo 150. Quo vero in loco, nisi in quibusdam Occidentis partibus viguerit, dici non potest, quia de ea silent omnino homines Græci, & certe est minuta hærefis, cuius ne Jsidorus quidem meminit, eam tamen amplexi sunt & retinet hodie Mahumetani, qui quenque in sua religione saluum fore docent, & credunt.

page.notes: The Greek word after "&" in "stupedam &" could not be read letter by letter; it is marked illegible. The first word "tasse" is a fragment at the line start and is marked uncertain. "Quisque" is read from a faint first line and may be imperfect. "perpe-rā" at the line end is uncertain. "fiuerit" is printed with a consonant u; I have set it as "fiverit" with [?]. "pafsim" is printed with an f-like long s; I have set it as "passim" with [?] implied by the printed form, and "passim" appears as printed without a mark. The top-left "Cap.72." is a chapter-and-page head and is not treated as a page number. The small mark at the bottom left is too faint to read and is left out. The end-of-chapter word "CAP." is taken as the catchword.
